run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Investigated the hotel-reservation namespace with Kubernetes objects/events, pod and Loki logs, Jaeger traces and Prometheus metrics, relying on the snapshot at 2026-11-21T10:20:16Z. The reservation request path shows no failure: all eight per-service blackbox probes (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user) return probe_success=1; sampled HTTP and gRPC spans return 200 in the millisecond range (e.g. trace 495cbda3d34e9708: GET /hotels 7.8ms, search 5.5ms, rate 4.0ms, geo 61us); all hotel-reservation endpoint objects report kube_endpoint_address_not_ready=0; no up==0 series exists for any hotel-reservation target; and the wrk2 generator shows stable rounds (~98 req/s, mean 3.3-3.4ms, max 10.5ms) with connect/read/write socket errors 0. The only alert at 10:20:16Z is KubePodNotReady (pending since 10:20:09Z) on pod audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd, which is not Ready because the CronJob's one-shot archiver container completed and terminated at 10:19:05Z while its fluent-bit-sidecar keeps running; this is a property of CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver, not of the reservation path. Two fault-injection artifacts exist (ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate mounted as /scripts into mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate, both rolled to new ReplicaSets at 10:18:22-24Z), but no evidence shows the scripts ran inside the window: no revokeRoles/dropUser output, admin authentication succeeded at 10:18:31/10:18:35Z, rate completed 2637/2637 requests with 0 rejected and 0 expired, and search recorded 3693 attempts with 0 failures and 0 timeouts. The only genuine application error is a one-shot startup crash of the search container (exit code 1, restarts 1) at 10:18:23Z because Consul was not yet listening on :8500; it re-registered at 10:18:24Z. Because the namespace itself was created at 10:18:19Z, no pre-incident baseline exists and no application fault was observed; whether a fault was intended later is unresolved, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: At 2026-11-21T10:20:16Z all eight hotel-reservation service probes return probe_success=1 (instances frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo...:8083, profile...:8081, rate...:8084, recommendation...:8085, reservation...:8087, search...:8082, user...:8086, job blackbox-hotel-reservation); the only probe returning 0 is job blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation instance http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=2015-04-09&outDate=2015-04-10&lat=38.0235&lon=-122.095.

For blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation the probe returned probe_http_status_code=0 with probe_dns_lookup_time_seconds=0.00271, probe_ip_addr_hash=0, probe_duration_seconds=0.00284 and probe_failed_due_to_regex=0, i.e. no HTTP response was obtained and no address was resolved.

Cumulative span counts at 10:20:16Z are frontend 12715, profile 7033, search 6219, reservation 6201, rate 4181, geo 2110, recommendation 1366, user 44, all under status_code=STATUS_CODE_UNSET; per operation the busiest are frontend /profile.Profile/GetProfiles 3497, frontend /search.Search/Nearby 2110, frontend HTTP GET /hotels 2110, geo /geo.Geo/Nearby 2110, rate /rate.Rate/GetRates 2059, reservation /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability 2059, frontend HTTP POST /reservation 24 and frontend HTTP POST /user 21.

Mean span duration since service start is sub-2ms per service (frontend 1.75ms, search 1.18ms, rate 0.27ms, profile 0.21ms, reservation 0.18ms, geo 0.10ms, recommendation 0.03ms, user 0.02ms); per operation the slowest paths are frontend HTTP POST /reservation 6.54ms (client MakeReservation 5.79ms vs server 5.20ms), frontend HTTP GET /hotels 4.08ms, search /search.Search/Nearby 1.79ms and rate mongo_rate 1.53ms.

Trace 495cbda3d34e9708 completes HTTP GET /hotels with http.status_code=200 in 7.8ms, composed of frontend->search /search.Search/Nearby 6.06ms, search server span 5.52ms containing /rate.Rate/GetRates 4.82ms (rate server 4.02ms with memcached_get_multi_rate 283us) and /geo.Geo/Nearby 0.67ms (geo server 61us), plus /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability 437us and /profile.Profile/GetProfiles 199us; the visible parent references form that chain and no span carries an error tag.

All five sampled traces of frontend HTTP POST /reservation returned http.status_code=200 (3.48-8.14ms) with reservation MakeReservation server spans 1.33-6.49ms and user CheckUser 0.66-0.95ms, and all five sampled traces of HTTP POST /user returned 200 (0.61-1.66ms).

The only alert present at 10:20:16Z is ALERTS{alertname="KubePodNotReady",namespace="hotel-reservation",pod="audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd",severity="critical"} value 1 with alertstate="pending"; ALERTS_FOR_STATE records its activeAt as epoch 1795256409 (10:20:09Z) and no other ALERTS series exists.

Pod audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd (created 10:19:00Z) has container archiver with ready=false, restartCount=0 and state terminated, and container fluent-bit-sidecar with ready=true and state running, while the pod phase is Running; that is the state kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"} reports for it.

CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver (schedule "* * * * *", suspend=false) runs an archiver container (busybox) that posts one record to 127.0.0.1:24224 and then exits, next to a fluent-bit-sidecar container running "nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat" that carries the sidecar's tcpSocket startupProbe on port 24224; because the sidecar keeps listening after the archiver exits, each Job pod stays Running but never Ready.

The archiver container of pod audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd logged "archiver: audit record forwarded" at 10:19:04Z and "archiver: upload complete (0 bytes archived); record=audit-archive-ready" at 10:19:05Z, and the same sequence succeeded in pod audit-log-archiver-29920940-8c54x at 10:20:04-10:20:05Z, so the archiving work completed and forwarding to the sidecar worked.

Pod audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd recorded a Warning event at 10:19:03Z: "Startup probe failed: dial tcp 10.244.234.144:24224: connect: connection refused", and the fluent-bit-sidecar logged binding to port 24224 at 10:19:03.42Z, i.e. the probe ran before the listener existed.

Container hotel-reserv-search in pod search-567bb6c4b8-wq6lr last terminated with exitCode 1 and reason Error at 10:18:23Z (restartCount 1), its log ending with FTL "failed register: Put http://consul:8500/v1/agent/service/register: dial tcp 10.96.169.7:8500: connect: connection refused"; the restarted instance logged "Successfully registered in consul" at 10:18:24Z.

Deployments hotel-reservation/mongodb-geo and hotel-reservation/mongodb-rate are at revision 2 and their live pod templates mount an extra volume "failure-script" (mountPath /scripts) from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, while the recorded kubectl last-applied-configuration for both Deployments lists no such volume; events show the first ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf scaled down and replaced by mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 at 10:18:22-10:18:24Z.

ConfigMap hotel-reservation/failure-admin-geo holds remove-admin-mongo.sh, revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh (revokeRolesFromUser readWrite on geo-db), revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh and remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh, and hotel-reservation/failure-admin-rate holds the equivalents targeting rate-db with ADMIN_USER=admin; these are the only fault-named ConfigMaps in the cluster.

Rate service counters at 10:20:16Z (instance rate.hotel-reservation:9091): rate_requests_received_total=2637, rate_requests_completed_total=2637, rate_requests_rejected_total=0, rate_requests_expired_total=0, rate_queue_depth=0, rate_in_flight=0, rate_backend_qps_limit=500, rate_queue_capacity=256.

Search service counters at 10:20:16Z (instance search.hotel-reservation:9092): search_requests_total=3693, search_rate_attempts_total=3693, search_rate_successes_total=3693, search_rate_failures_total=0, search_rate_timeouts_total=0, so search's calls to rate recorded no failures or timeouts.

MongoDB logs show admin authentication succeeding from the application pods on mongodb-rate at 10:18:31.252Z and 10:18:35.467Z (SCRAM-SHA-1, principalName=admin, remote 10.244.7.234) and on mongodb-geo at 10:18:31.054Z/10:18:31.127Z (remote 10.244.7.232); a log search over both pods for drop/createUser/grantRoles/revokeRoles in 10:18:16-10:20:16Z returned only the init-script output at 10:18:28-10:18:29Z, i.e. no privilege-changing command was executed in the window.

Every hotel-reservation endpoint object reports kube_endpoint_address_not_ready=0 (consul, frontend, geo, jaeger-out, memcached-profile/-rate/-reserve, mongodb-geo/-profile/-rate/-recommendation/-reservation/-user, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user).

The wrk2 load generator in hotel-reservation reports three consecutive stable rounds against the frontend: 2934 requests in 30.02s (97.74 req/s) with timeout 187, then 2971 requests in 30.03s and 2971 requests in 30.04s (98.92 req/s) with timeout 195 each, mean latency 3.30-3.42ms and max 6.75-10.46ms, connect/read/write socket errors all 0 and no Non-2xx response lines.

All hotel-reservation pods carry creationTimestamp between 10:18:20Z and 10:19:00Z (e.g. frontend-68745cb99c-lfp95, rate-65d6967c95-lrwch, search-567bb6c4b8-wq6lr, mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-njc2c created 10:18:24Z, mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-scl6k created 10:18:24Z), and the event stream shows those Deployments being scaled up from 0 to 1 with image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation:sha-d2c036bc3d1138f5a0bdaffd3d87f37522c3461a at 10:18:20-10:18:24Z, so every observed metric and trace post-dates the deployment.

No container in the namespace is CPU-throttled or CPU-bound at 10:20:16Z: the throttling ratio is 0 for every hotel-reservation container except mongodb-rate at 0.0069 and pod-level mongodb-user at 0.0041, per-pod CPU usage tops out at 0.087 cores (frontend) with search 0.046 and rate 0.035, and node CPU utilisation is 0.41-0.52.

The up==0 query returns 41 failed scrape targets, none of them in namespace hotel-reservation (they are tidb-cluster, slack-spine, frappe, saleor, astronomy-shop and train-ticket instances), and the hotel-reservation-application job has 2 up targets (search.hotel-reservation:9092 and rate.hotel-reservation:9091) with lastError empty.

The hypothesis that the staged database-privilege fault (failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo) was active by 10:20:16Z is contradicted by rate completing all 2637 received requests with 0 rejected and 0 expired, by search recording 0 rate failures and 0 rate timeouts over 3693 attempts, by continuous successful admin authentication and healthy mongo_rate/mongo_profile client spans (63 and 59 calls at 1.53ms and 0.91ms mean), and by the absence of any revokeRoles/dropUser command output in the mongodb logs during 10:18:16-10:20:16Z.

The hypothesis of a pod-level resource fault (OOM, eviction, restart storm) is contradicted at 10:20:16Z: all hotel-reservation pods are Running with restartCount 0 except search (1, from the 10:18:23Z startup crash), no container reports OOMKilled or any other last-terminated reason besides search's Error, and the only non-running container state in the namespace is the audit-log-archiver archiver container that terminated after finishing its upload.

The KubePodNotReady alert on audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd is a design consequence of the audit-log-archiver CronJob pod template (one-shot archiver container plus long-running fluent-bit-sidecar) rather than degradation of the reservation request path: the archiver finished successfully at 10:19:05Z, yet the running sidecar keeps the pod from ever becoming Ready, and consecutive Jobs 29920939 through 29920943 all show ready=0 with active=1.

The failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe most likely reflects a monitoring target with no backing Ingress in this cluster (no HTTP status, no resolved address, 2.8ms duration) rather than a fault of the frontend, which answered every probed path with HTTP 200; I could not read any Ingress object, so the absence of an Ingress is unverified.

The single search container crash at 10:18:23Z is a startup-ordering race rather than a lasting failure: search started at 10:18:23-10:18:24Z while Consul (pod created 10:18:20Z, Raft election at 10:18:22Z) was not yet serving :8500, so the registration call was refused and the process exited with code 1; it restarted, registered at 10:18:24Z, and its later counters show no failures.

A database-privilege fault was apparently prepared for this run via the staged failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate scripts, but if so it had not been applied by 10:20:16Z: the mongo pods show only their 10:18:28-10:18:35Z startup authentications, no later shell exec connection or privilege command, and no consumer-visible impact.

gaps: No telemetry precedes the deployment: the hotel-reservation namespace was created at 2026-11-21T10:18:19Z (my namespace listing view for that fact is not citable here) and all pods date from 10:18:20-10:19:00Z, so there is no pre-incident baseline and no latency trend can be inferred.

Prometheus returned only the single sample at 2026-11-21T10:20:16Z for the range queries I ran (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[1h]) and rate_backend_qps_limit produced one point), so per-minute rates over the window could not be reconstructed and the 187-195 wrk2 socket timeouts per 30s round have no earlier baseline to compare against.

Jaeger retained only the newest traces: the sampled spans start around 10:20:05-10:20:15Z (trace source_start_at 10:20:15.84-10:20:15.89Z), so traces cannot describe the 10:18-10:20Z period, and trace span counts are not request counts.
The traces_search for frontend over 09:20-10:20Z was returned as RESULT_TOO_LARGE and only a 60-row slice was read (369 spans existed), so the trace view is a sample, not a complete picture.
A query for span series with status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" returned no data (status no_data), so the absence of error-status spans is not proven; only STATUS_CODE_UNSET series were observed.

The Ingress listing returned an empty, non-citable result (status no_data) and the ResourceQuota and NetworkPolicy listings returned empty results, so I can only say those queries matched nothing; I cannot prove that no Ingress, quota or NetworkPolicy exists.

MongoDB secrets and the live user/role state cannot be read, so I could not directly verify whether the admin user still holds readWrite on geo-db or rate-db; I only observed that no revoke command was logged and authentication plus queries kept working.

Whether a fault-injection action was scheduled after 2026-11-21T10:20:16Z (outside the authorized window) is unknown, as is which staged ConfigMap (failure-admin-geo or failure-admin-rate) the run intended to use.
No change_history integration is available in this Run, so the actor and time of the 10:18:22-10:18:24Z mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate template changes could not be confirmed from a change record.

Several views were incomplete or truncated (the frontend trace slice, the trace searches for HTTP POST /reservation and POST /user, the search pod log read of 250 of 262 lines, the Loki namespace scan limited to 20 newest lines and the wrk2 Loki scan limited to 40 newest lines), so those reads state limits on what was seen rather than complete coverage.

The Kafka, blackbox-ingress and audit-log-archiver unread objects (no ingress-nginx deployment, no Job pod logs inside 10:18:16-10:20:16Z for pod audit-log-archiver-29920941-8r56j) remain unread gaps.
next_steps: Confirm with the platform or harness owner which fault scenario was scheduled for this run and when it was applied; the only fault-named objects are ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate in namespace hotel-reservation.

If a database-privilege fault is expected, re-check mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo after client connections are recycled (authentication is per connection) and inspect the admin user's roles directly (e.g. db.getUser('admin')) instead of inferring from request counters.

Review the audit-log-archiver CronJob in namespace hotel-reservation: let the Job complete (sidecar that exits, or a restartable sidecar pattern) or exclude completed Job pods from KubePodNotReady so the pending alert stops recurring every minute.

Fix or remove the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe target http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels, which obtains no HTTP status or address and therefore always reports probe_success=0.

Add Consul-registration retry/backoff to the search service (and any other service that fatally exits when Consul is unreachable) so a container does not crash when it starts before the Consul HTTP API on :8500 is listening.

Pod audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd recorded a Warning event at 10:19:03Z: "Startup probe failed: dial tcp 10.244.234.144:24224: connect: connection refused", and the fluent-bit-sidecar logged binding to port 24224 at 10:19:03.42Z, i.e. the probe ran before the listener existed.

Container hotel-reserv-search in pod search-567bb6c4b8-wq6lr last terminated with exitCode 1 and reason Error at 10:18:23Z (restartCount 1), its log ending with FTL "failed register: Put http://consul:8500/v1/agent/service/register: dial tcp 10.96.169.7:8500: connect: connection refused"; the restarted instance logged "Successfully registered in consul" at 10:18:24Z.

Deployments hotel-reservation/mongodb-geo and hotel-reservation/mongodb-rate are at revision 2 and their live pod templates mount an extra volume "failure-script" (mountPath /scripts) from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, while the recorded kubectl last-applied-configuration for both Deployments lists no such volume; events show the first ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf scaled down and replaced by mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 at 10:18:22-10:18:24Z.

ConfigMap hotel-reservation/failure-admin-geo holds remove-admin-mongo.sh, revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh (revokeRolesFromUser readWrite on geo-db), revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh and remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh, and hotel-reservation/failure-admin-rate holds the equivalents targeting rate-db with ADMIN_USER=admin; these are the only fault-named ConfigMaps in the cluster.

Rate service counters at 10:20:16Z (instance rate.hotel-reservation:9091): rate_requests_received_total=2637, rate_requests_completed_total=2637, rate_requests_rejected_total=0, rate_requests_expired_total=0, rate_queue_depth=0, rate_in_flight=0, rate_backend_qps_limit=500, rate_queue_capacity=256.

Search service counters at 10:20:16Z (instance search.hotel-reservation:9092): search_requests_total=3693, search_rate_attempts_total=3693, search_rate_successes_total=3693, search_rate_failures_total=0, search_rate_timeouts_total=0, so search's calls to rate recorded no failures or timeouts.

MongoDB logs show admin authentication succeeding from the application pods on mongodb-rate at 10:18:31.252Z and 10:18:35.467Z (SCRAM-SHA-1, principalName=admin, remote 10.244.7.234) and on mongodb-geo at 10:18:31.054Z/10:18:31.127Z (remote 10.244.7.232); a log search over both pods for drop/createUser/grantRoles/revokeRoles in 10:18:16-10:20:16Z returned only the init-script output at 10:18:28-10:18:29Z, i.e. no privilege-changing command was executed in the window.

Every hotel-reservation endpoint object reports kube_endpoint_address_not_ready=0 (consul, frontend, geo, jaeger-out, memcached-profile/-rate/-reserve, mongodb-geo/-profile/-rate/-recommendation/-reservation/-user, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user).

The wrk2 load generator in hotel-reservation reports three consecutive stable rounds against the frontend: 2934 requests in 30.02s (97.74 req/s) with timeout 187, then 2971 requests in 30.03s and 2971 requests in 30.04s (98.92 req/s) with timeout 195 each, mean latency 3.30-3.42ms and max 6.75-10.46ms, connect/read/write socket errors all 0 and no Non-2xx response lines.

All hotel-reservation pods carry creationTimestamp between 10:18:20Z and 10:19:00Z (e.g. frontend-68745cb99c-lfp95, rate-65d6967c95-lrwch, search-567bb6c4b8-wq6lr, mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-njc2c created 10:18:24Z, mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-scl6k created 10:18:24Z), and the event stream shows those Deployments being scaled up from 0 to 1 with image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation:sha-d2c036bc3d1138f5a0bdaffd3d87f37522c3461a at 10:18:20-10:18:24Z, so every observed metric and trace post-dates the deployment.

No container in the namespace is CPU-throttled or CPU-bound at 10:20:16Z: the throttling ratio is 0 for every hotel-reservation container except mongodb-rate at 0.0069 and pod-level mongodb-user at 0.0041, per-pod CPU usage tops out at 0.087 cores (frontend) with search 0.046 and rate 0.035, and node CPU utilisation is 0.41-0.52.

The up==0 query returns 41 failed scrape targets, none of them in namespace hotel-reservation (they are tidb-cluster, slack-spine, frappe, saleor, astronomy-shop and train-ticket instances), and the hotel-reservation-application job has 2 up targets (search.hotel-reservation:9092 and rate.hotel-reservation:9091) with lastError empty.

hypothesis.text: The KubePodNotReady alert on audit-log-archiver-29920939-p87cd is a design consequence of the audit-log-archiver CronJob pod template (one-shot archiver container plus long-running fluent-bit-sidecar) rather than degradation of the reservation request path: the archiver finished successfully at 10:19:05Z, yet the running sidecar keeps the pod from ever becoming Ready, and consecutive Jobs 29920939 through 29920943 all show ready=0 with active=1.

The failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe most likely reflects a monitoring target with no backing Ingress in this cluster (no HTTP status, no resolved address, 2.8ms duration) rather than a fault of the frontend, which answered every probed path with HTTP 200; I could not read any Ingress object, so the absence of an Ingress is unverified.

The single search container crash at 10:18:23Z is a startup-ordering race rather than a lasting failure: search started at 10:18:23-10:18:24Z while Consul (pod created 10:18:20Z, Raft election at 10:18:22Z) was not yet serving :8500, so the registration call was refused and the process exited with code 1; it restarted, registered at 10:18:24Z, and its later counters show no failures.

A database-privilege fault was apparently prepared for this run via the staged failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate scripts, but if so it had not been applied by 10:20:16Z: the mongo pods show only their 10:18:28-10:18:35Z startup authentications, no later shell exec connection or privilege command, and no consumer-visible impact.

counter_evidence.text: The hypothesis that the staged database-privilege fault (failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo) was active by 10:20:16Z is contradicted by rate completing all 2637 received requests with 0 rejected and 0 expired, by search recording 0 rate failures and 0 rate timeouts over 3693 attempts, by continuous successful admin authentication and healthy mongo_rate/mongo_profile client spans (63 and 59 calls at 1.53ms and 0.91ms mean), and by the absence of any revokeRoles/dropUser command output in the mongodb logs during 10:18:16-10:20:16Z.

The hypothesis of a pod-level resource fault (OOM, eviction, restart storm) is contradicted at 10:20:16Z: all hotel-reservation pods are Running with restartCount 0 except search (1, from the 10:18:23Z startup crash), no container reports OOMKilled or any other last-terminated reason besides search's Error, and the only non-running container state in the namespace is the audit-log-archiver archiver container that terminated after finishing its upload.

containers.name: archiver
command:
set -eu
record="${AUDIT_ARCHIVE_RECORD:-audit-archive-ready}"
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: starting audit log archive"
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: bundling /var/log/audit"
attempt=0
until reply=$(printf "%s\n" "$record" | nc -w 2 127.0.0.1 24224) && [ "$reply" = "$record" ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  if [ "$attempt" -ge 10 ]; then
    echo "archiver: log forwarding unavailable" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
done
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: audit record forwarded"
sleep 1
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: upload complete (0 bytes archived); record=$record"

data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \

  sleep 1

     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"
